chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Les Brown arrangement and first stint with Lionel Hampton
summary: A lost arrangement for Les Brown; Glaser sent McRae to Boston for two weeks with Hampton, and Dexter Gordon's departure kept him on.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: we don't even put a name on -- till we record it and see what it sounds like. "What are you gonna call this," you know. "Oh, we'll call this 'Stomp Off,' or something like that. That we wrote for Les Brown. That was never recorded because the arrangement got lost. We sent it out to California, they never did find the arrangement on it.
So, Les Brown was one of the --
One of the things, yeah. I -- in fact Joe --
Joe Glaser wanted me to join Les Brown after I got through with Louie -- after, I mean Hamp. See, when I went up to Boston to join Lionel Hampton for a couple of weeks --
This is the first time you joined Lionel Hampton.
Yeah, the first time I joined

Lionel. I was supposed to be there for a couple of weeks until Arnie Cobb's shoulder got better. Him and Dexter was wrestling in the dressing room, and, you know, Cobb being so heavy, he bumped his shoulder on the door.
Then that was an excuse for him to take off a couple of weeks, you know.
And Hamp told Glaser to send me up there, you know. So Glaser say go up to Boston, stay two weeks with Hampton and come back because I want you to go out with Les Brown.
(Inaudible) heard about me, (say inaudible) put me in the band.
Well Hamp talked to Glaser and begged me to stay on, because Dexter Gordon --
When Hamp was coming back, Dexter Gordon say I'm leaving. So that left the chair open, a couple so I just stayed on (inaudible) years.
